title: Edge of the Cape
subtitle: That's a dark shade of blue.

items.text: Edge of the Cape
Night falls, and Diggers sits on a bench by the river, holding a cheap takeout box.
He stuffs his mouth with food.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: *munch*

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Could it be that Sophia can reverse time with her arcane skill?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Or is this just a big illusion that I've conjured up?
Woof, woof!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Aww! A puppy!
The puppy's wet eyes are fixed to the meat on his fork.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Go on, eat up.
In the quiet night, the evening star twinkles above the dark purple horizon.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I guess it doesn't really matter how I'm back here, no strange languages, no strange doctrines.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So, for now, I'll continue spreading my art, speaking out for those who pursue "peace and love."

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But …
He falls silent, an unusual occurrence.
A gust of night wind blows a crumpled poster to his feet.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: "A grand art gathering coming soon to Carnaby Street!"

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: "An unprecedented arcanum feast, an unparalleled grand march."

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: "Against war, against everything!"
The exaggerated slogans pique his interest.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh! I need to do more. People trust actions more than words.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: This is where I'm needed.
This is what he excels at.
There is no need for preparation. It all flows naturally and seamlessly.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: London needs imaginative art parties. It needs street fairs for everyone to get their voice heard.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: London is utopian.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I will throw a feast for more people to have fun. By then, our philosophy will hit the headlines of all newspapers and become a new tidal trend. Everyone will get to know and fall in love!
Countless dream bubbles float in the air, reflecting rainbow colors under the sunlight.
Dreamlike visions bloom within them.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Everyone will see that world.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: No violence, no hatred.
He is lost in his own fervor.
A flamboyant artist, and a narrow-minded egotist.
The culprit who caused utter chaos with his Reflective Bubbles.
Until a car speeds up to him.

items.speaker: Car
items.text: *beep*
The brakes screech, but it is too late.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Whoa!
The artist's frail body is flung high into the air, crashing down hard.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ah!
The panicked scream echoes off the cavern walls.
He sits up abruptly, wiping the cold sweat from his forehead with trembling hands.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Huff—huff—

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It was just a dream!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I even came up with the newspaper headline.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: "Pioneer Artist Dies for Peace and Love."

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Or maybe it should read: "Chaos Instigator Dies, Peace Restored to London."

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: If I'm lucky, they might even include some of my ideas.
Sometimes, he envies the famous; all they have to do is speak, and their thoughts are spread far and wide by their followers.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: *sigh*
He gets up, almost tripping over the fabric.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, the islander's robe.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I guess I should put this on, then get out of here.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Leave this island, leave Manus Vindictae, leave all their organizations and hierarchies, and continue my art.
He dons the white robe.
The escape from the cave is surprisingly straightforward.
All the critical checkpoints are unguarded.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hmm, where is everyone?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Are they all at another maths class?
Aren't you leaving?
Diggers takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hey, my friend.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We bathe in the light of Apollo's star, following a fixed rhythm, balancing the excess of our souls.
His acting skills have slightly improved.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So, could you point me in the direction of the ferry?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I want to ... um … go to the real world ... to find those … uh … fragments.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: I don't quite understand what you're saying.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: But if you want to leave, you can come with us.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Wonderful. You must be a very generous number.
The believer gives him a strange look.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: We're not numbers.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: Those gathered here are either fractions or those who haven't yet discovered their soul numbers.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: That's why we're leaving this place, where only integers can live with full rights.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Then we're on the same page!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It's rare to find like-minded people on this little island. So, where are we headed now?

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: Forward.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: A lady promised us that the envoy would be waiting ahead to meet us.

items.speaker: Island Believer II
items.text: At the end of the cape.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Take me with you. Please take me with you.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I believe that art isn't dead yet!
